title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Framework for Global Total Electron Content Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2610.37159v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Accurate forecasting of global total electron content (TEC) is important for space weather monitoring and the reliable operation of satellite communication and navigation systems. We propose a physics-guided generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework for day-ahead global TEC forecasting. The framework builds on flow matching, which learns to gradually transform samples from an initial distribution into new samples that share the statistical characteristics of the target data. The proposed model incorporates ionospheric dynamics described by a partial differential equation (PDE) into this transformation process, guiding the changes between initial and target samples using physical knowledge. The model further combines the physical dynamics with statistical patterns captured from data to learn this transformation, adaptively adjusting their relative contributions at each location. The model is trained and evaluated using one year

translated_title: 物理引导的流匹配：一种用于全球总电子含量预测的生成式人工智能框架
translated_abstract: 准确预测全球总电子含量（TEC）对于空间天气监测以及卫星通信和导航系统的可靠运行至关重要。我们提出了一种物理引导的生成式人工智能（AI）框架，用于次日全球TEC预测。该框架建立在流匹配的基础上，流匹配学习将样本从初始分布逐步变换为具有目标数据统计特性的新样本。所提出的模型将偏微分方程（PDE）所描述的电离层动力学纳入这一变换过程，利用物理知识引导初始样本与目标样本之间的变化。该模型进一步将物理动力学与从数据中捕获的统计模式相结合来学习这一变换，并在每个位置自适应地调整二者的相对贡献。该模型使用一年的数据进行训练和评估。
tldr: 提出了一种物理引导的流匹配生成式AI框架，将偏微分方程描述的电离层动力学与数据驱动的统计模式自适应融合，实现次日全球总电子含量预测。
en_tdlr: A physics-guided flow matching framework that adaptively integrates PDE-based ionospheric dynamics with data-driven statistical patterns for day-ahead global TEC forecasting.
